notes.title: Content Update on Main!
notes.notes:
The content update is now on main! Most people were already playing the beta through the sale, so thank you to everyone! Let me know if any issues pop up in the forum, but everything appears to be clear!

New additions:

-2 new support items! These need to be unlocked by engaging with the new map content.

-New map type: Pilgrims gate. Highly defended regions that show up later in runs.

-3 New POIs, two unique to the Pilgrims gate, another that is always/multiples common in asteroid belts, occasionally elsewhere.

-2 new cargo ships, both appearing mid-late in runs. A third cargo exclusive to the Pilgrims gate.

-Cargo ships now can have escorts.

-Minor loot Poi that drops health and a small cache of coins that can appear in place of empty POI slots.

Minor additions/changes:

-Alien Fighter Select Screen now mentions the rolls have iframes

-Ship HP and Speed added to the ship select screen, as these vary by ship

-Audio fix for alien cargo plasma castor, missed in the audio fixing update.

notes.title: Content update nearing completion
notes.notes:
I am in the final stages of the content update I've been working on for Broadside Renegades and I am very satisfied with the results so far. All that's left is internal testing and some art polishing. I won't promise a specific date yet as the day job has been demanding but it will be on the beta branch #soon should all things go smoothly.

The update will contain:

-1 new map type with its own major and minor unique POI and a unique cargo ship 

-2 new general cargo ship types

-Cargo escorts (the first combat ship for the civ faction)

-New minor unmarked loot POI

-2 new support items

-1 new active POI that is common on asteroid fields (at least one always) and rare on some other map types (2+ would be very rare but not impossible). Happy with how these interact when there is multiple.

The next time I post about the update should hopefully to be to announce its on the beta branch (or something awful has happened)!

notes.title: Things are in progress
notes.notes:
Good day pirates!

I don't have a time frame yet, but now that the demo has been polished, I've begun toying with some new ideas and content for the first post launch content update!

I won't spoil anything yet, but the first main focus is on cargo ships. You probably spend the most time attacking these, so it only makes sense to throw some wrinkles in your raiding. Expect more resistance (and more reward). Some of this is already in on my end and being tested.

Secondly, I want to squeeze in a few more POIs into the same update to increase map/run variety in general. These are still more in the planning phase, with some art done, but subject to change. I currently have art and a plan for a smaller one (like the mined cache) and some of the art and a vague idea for 2 larger ones (like the scavenger depots, something with active NPC map activity related to it). There's no hard floor or ceiling on these, just whatever I can come up with and test in a timely manner, so I don't feature creep what I have already.

Minimally one item is finished and in the testing phase (related to cargo content, they get a new toy, you should too). A second item is actually in and just needs some retesting, as I hadn't realized I never made an achievement to unlock it at 1.0. I may review a few other disabled items or weapons to determine if I can bring them up to quality, but they are also in the "feature creep" camp. So minimally 2 new support/yellow items should be here as well.

I'll tease more as I have more in (hopefully I'm bad at marketing)

notes.title: Demo V2 update

The demo now has:

-a preview of the upgrades screen

I know this is boring news for those who already own the game, but the good news is this is out of the way. I have a few bits of unfinished content that never made it into 1.0, so I'm looking at minimally restoring some of that next.

notes.title: Mouse V2 Update on Main
notes.notes:
The mouse steering v2 update it here!

Main changes:
-you can now warp, pickup items, and use items all using the mouse steering mode, enabling one handed gameplay with either hand (or a combo of the two).
-mouse steering is now offered in the tutorial if not enabled. It's become my default preference, and it shouldn't be hidden in the menu

Minor:
-ship select screen more clearly supports the mouse functionality
-switch ship selection using the scroll wheel, in addition to clicking the squares below ships to choose

notes.title: One more beta tweak, now testing for main
notes.notes:
Last quick push to the beta branch for mouse steering V2:

Ship select screen:

-scroll wheel can now move through ship select screen
-changed the launch button to make it's clickable-ness less vague
-better centering on launch button for aesthetic

Tutorial:

-Tutorial now prompts players to try mouse steering mode if it isn't active, resetting the tutorials movement phase
-Follow up asks whether to keep the option active (and saves the setting if one selects "Yes"). 


I considered making mouse steering the default at this point, but I figured the best option was to explicitly offer it in the tutorial. notes.title: Mouse Update V2 in the public beta branch
notes.notes:
I am pleased to announce mouse update V2 is on the beta branch. This hasn't been tested yet as heavily as the other updates but no changes were made to save data or files so this shouldn't pose any risk to your progress. The main goal here was to polish mouse controls so you can totally play the game without the keyboard if you fancy (you can still combine mouse steering with keyboard controls).

QoL:
-you can now click to end the mouse placement delay early after upgrading your ship

Currently there are no in game explanations or descriptions in the beta, but the new optional controls are as follows:

-Holding the middle mouse wheel will now use consumables. Single clicking will still use your 3rd ability.

-A small dead zone box has been placed around the ship while mouse steering is active. The mouse will no longer steer the ship inside this deadzone. This will prevent weird movement when moving the mouse across the ship quickly intending to turn around (less wobbly).

-left clicking inside this dead zone will now work like the "interact key" which is currently used to swap consumables and held down to warp.

notes.title: Sound stabilization update
notes.notes:
Bringing the newest build to the default branch. This may or may not effect you based on your system, but this should make sounds behave more predictably across the board, especially when many sounds are going at once. Volume settings should feel more impactful and reliable than before. 

The warp ready sound has been made to slightly overpower the other sounds, as I have had some feedback that it was easy to miss that a warp was ready. I'll change this if people find it annoying, but it feels like an important noise to lose in the cannon fire, let me know!

Also, a bugfix for the Art of Destruction that stops the player from selecting a 7th support item not displayed on the GUI.

notes.title: Sound balancing beta update
notes.notes:
Good voyages space pirates! Update to the beta branch containing:

-Major pass on sound balancing. Sounds should be more respectful of your audio settings and less likely to conflict when many sounds are playing. I believe I've tracked down and update the vast majority of sounds. Any that still seem off for anybody would be greatly appreciated!

-Fix for the Art of Destruction allowing a 7th support item not displayed on the GUI. As the only ship that starts with a support item vs the normal weapon item, it wasn't aware one of its slots was already occupied. 

This update should be release ready, but I have finished migrating everything to a new PC. Will likely do more redundant general testing to ensure no arcane changes have happened behind the scenes. Public beta access if you'd like to try it now, especially if sounds seemed off before.

notes.title: Mouse Update on Main
notes.notes:
It's finally here! I am happy to announce the mouse update has arrived. 

Some of the most common feedback has been to add a mouse option to the game, and today it's here. The mouse can be used for abilities, and speed controlled via the scroll wheel. These can be used in any combination with the keyboard (if you still to prefer to WASD steer and fire abilities with the mouse, now you can). 

In addition, under settings, you can enable mouse steering mode, which will cause ships to always turn towards the mouse cursor. Personally this has become my main mode of playing the game, and I'm happy with how it has turned out.

Lastly, the most arduous/least exciting part on the backend, all menus have been rewritten to allow mouse navigation. 

Happy cargo hunting space pirates!

notes.title: Mouse Update on the public beta
notes.notes:
I'm happy to announce the mouse update is now on the public beta branch!

All menus should work now with the mouse, clicking once to select an option and again to continue. Under control options, you can now turn on "Mouse steering", which will cause the ship to automatically turn to face the mouse cursor. I'm very happy with how this turned out and may consider it my preferred way to play now. The mouse buttons are now also bound to abilities, while the scroll wheel can be used to accelerate or decelerate. The player can use any combination of mouse and keyboard (mouse buttons all still work when mouse steering is off).

Still needs a little more polishing, and there are currently no in game explanations of the new options, but that will be coming next before it makes it into the default branch.

notes.title: Progress Report 09/23/24
notes.notes:
Good evening! 

Due to popular demand, I have paused the tutorial update to add in mouse support. Initially I had focused on the keyboard for simplicity and keeping the controls centralized (on the default bindings), but I've had the most requests for some kind of mouse support.

The good news is that the in game portion is prototyped and working at about 70%. Mouse steering is an optional new way to control your ship, controlling speed with mouse wheel, abilities with the clicks, and  the ship orientating itself towards the mouse cursor. The steering portion will be toggled, as it wont be everyone's cup of tea, but mouse buttons will always work, allowing you to use both if you still wish to steer via WASD but fire your weapons via mouse clicks, etc. The upgrade menu has been converted to allow for either, and will give you a 2 second pause to relocate your mouse if you have mouse steering active (so selecting something doesn't swerve you into a missile when it closes).

I hope to have this portion on the beta in the near future, with a bit more testing.

The bad news is, converting the rest of the menus will *probably* take a little longer, as they werent designed for that from scratch, but I intend to fully integrate the mouse for consistency sake. 

I'm on the fence whether to push all the new QoL features to an updated demo after this update is completed, or to wait for the full tutorial/onboarding upgrade to be finished. The demo is already outdated, based on a build from June, so it needs a refresh ASAP. On the other hand, I'd like to only really work on it one more stretch (aside from bugs etc) so I can focus any future updates on the main game.

notes.title: Update 1.052 Easy difficulty, balance and QoL
notes.notes:
Moving the build to the stable main branch, no known issues currently

[b]Phase 1 changes:[/b]

-There is now an "Easy" difficulty. This can be tweaked further, but currently it reduces enemy spawn banks by roughly 30% across the board. It will still ramp up near the final boss, but should slow down the first few levels. It also reduces most enemy damage and fire rates by 40%, as well as collision damage from crashing into other ships.

-Added a L and R indicator (that can be switched off) under the graphical options. This should help with people's orientation when using broadside weapons.

[b]Major addition:[/b]

-There are now ending scenes that reflect the players chosen captain. These will now happen when you warp away from the final boss, instead of just cutting to the stats screen. The stats screen will now also reflect if you die after defeating the final boss, but without warping home.

[b]Crash fixs:[/b]

-Fixed a rare crash when reverting to default keybinds and then attempting to switch controller modes.

As always, post any bugs in the Steam forum, that's the fastest way to get a hold of me.
[b]
Small tweaks/balance:[/b]

-Greatly increased acceleration/deceleration of the Vow of Poverty, making it control a lot more responsively. Changing directions will no longer feel sluggish. A similar ship would be a prime candidate for a 3rd starter ship, as this would be an option for players that don't like boat controls, not locked behind game progress (and give two non-boat style options for variety).

-Fixed an issue with the Art of Destruction ship, which caused it's "goal speed" to remain at the boost level, causing hiccups if you attempted to decelerate after a boost for rapid turning.

-Buffed Energy Lance damage across the board by a small amount. Should make it more useful on/against faster ships, as contact time with enemies was lower than anticipated.

-Changed "Standard" to "Launch" in the menu for clarity against difficulty selection (as standard sounds like "medium", not "begin a run" in this context.


Next up, for phase 2 of onboarding plans, the focus will be on improving the tutorial to better explain concepts not immediately apparent. Then I'll be updating the demo with the collected QoL suggestions and feedback incorporated since launch.

notes.title: What's next
notes.notes:
First and foremost, thank you everyone for playing my game! Also thank you to everyone who's given me feedback, it's always helpful and welcome!

Started my day job back up Monday, and taking a few days this week to mentally recover (launch takes a toll, as exciting as it is). I'm now starting to formulate what the future entails for both me and Broadside Renegades. 

First and foremost, the main negative feedback (and looking at achievement data) is that the game is either too hard, or not doing a good job of on-boarding players. The combination of ship like controls, and the nature of the more "hit and run" style of broadside combat is thrust upon the player, and ramps up quickly once it starts. I have three (or all) possible avenues in the short term to address this:

1. A ship designed to offload the broadsiding while you learn to steer. I'm considering a 3rd starting ship, probably that controls like the first. I am still brainstorming, but imagining it having either autofiring, or partially autoaiming broadsides. This would allow players to get a hang of steering before having to learn steering AND timing shots at the same time. I am also trying to find a way to present the ship in a way that explains it is "easier" without discouraging players from trying it.

2. An outright easier difficulty. I actually have a ton of control over scaling, spawning, and even some unused built in multipliers (ie enemy damage -50%). This would be very little work. It's really a menu and some variables away. (This also means I can go the other way, but I'm not sure anyone's asking for that yet)

3. Expanded tutorial or practice room. This ones the largest undertaking, but will most likely happen in addition to the first two. Currently the tutorial explains the basics, but then thrusts you into the main game at full difficulty before you've gotten to use your new knowledge. I'm thinking of adding an intermediate level with some real enemies and cargo ships to get a hang of things better in. The big thing will be expanding how I present the player knowledge here. There's some tactics that probably arent immediately apparent, like how POI grant more gold the farther you warp, or that warping resets a portion of your threat level (buying you time, you arent expected to beat bosses when they first show up, run!).

I don't want to make grand promises yet, but in addition to this, in general my list also consists of:

1. Adding a ui element for "right" and "left" that turns with the ship. I could say port and starboard but that isn't helping the onboarding process.

2. New map type, that just needs an asset or two to make sense adding

3. I am going to test a new boss at some point, but will only add it if it is good. The idea is a bit elaborate so I'll need to see how it plays

4. I have some work done today on a very simple "cutscene/end graphic." I had cut the idea near launch, but I want to add a little more weight to winning. 

5. I actually have a small cache of content that is almost finished, or even actually finished and disabled in game. As this is my first launch, I leaned on minimal bugs or crashing, and put a lock on adding new content early. I still do art for leisure, and some things were WIP, so there's things that it wouldn't make sense not to get in the game.

If you've read this far, thank you! I try to check the community hub often so it's a good place to reach me!

notes.title: Patch 1.031 Perm Upgrade Cost Rebalancing, Polishing and Qol
notes.notes:
Update 1.031 is now pushed to the main branch, same changes. Any issues, please let me know here or in the bug reporting thread

Balance:
-Biggest change due to the most commonly received feedback. Permanent upgrades are now much cheaper, with the largest reductions to the first tier of each upgrade. The intention was never to create a grind, and new players were taking too many runs to get even the cheapest upgrade. This was an oversight due to the test players being really really good at the game now. My math was based on the 2-4k average gold per VICTORY, forgetting that the unusual play style of the game can see new players dying before 100. Moving between the beta and the standard should preserve your upgrade level (even if you buy cheap with the beta and move back to the main branch). The costs are internally coded and save files are unaffected by the update.

-Buffed flak cannons. Every time I watch someone new play I get nervous it was a bad pick, meaning it was much too weak. It gets stronger as the game goes on naturally, as more enemies exist to be hit by it. I was tempted to rewrite them with some targeting but it's the only totally random AOE weapon currently.

Now it deals slightly more damage and has an extra shell in every level of its volley. It might get more love after testing/feedback

QoL:
-Resuming the game with a controller will no longer trigger a ships 3rd ability

-Controller menu is now an image of a controller instead of a wall of text.

-Warp ready prompt now displays the key/controller button for 'interact' instead of the word 'interact'. I even found myself occasionally using an item when I meant to warp.

-Fixed an event forcing the comms dialogue in the tutorial to disappear fast.

-continuing to hunt down more inconsistent audio volume

-Bosses should no longer spawn on top of you if you are close to a warp gate. Smaller enemies are less likely to now. The bosses size made them feel unfair as they dwarf the gates in most cases.

-The Tank ship now has a funny name instead of "name WIP tank ship"

-Increased accept input delay when the upgrade menu pops up to prevent accidental selections in tense combat

notes.title: Demo Now Available!
notes.notes:
Calling all space pirates, the Broadside Renegades demo is now available! 

I've made 2 of my favorite ships open for play, The Widows Lament and The Shooting Star. 

The first is a light destroyer capable of dishing out and taking a decent amount of punishment. Once you master the timing of your broadsides, this ship will carry you to pirate glory! 

The second is a high skill ceiling fighter that must deploy to fire its rail gun and shock shield, but can outpace anything the enemy will throw at you in flight mode. The fire rate of additional weapons is faster the slower you fly, allowing you to focus on dodging at a high speed or slowing to unleash your fury.

While the basic goal of the demo is to defeat the Royal Watch capital carrier, you may continue to survive endlessly upon it's defeat. You don't have to fight it immediately once it arrives, and warping to the next sector will reset some of your threat level and buy you time to power up.

Go on now and become a Broadside Renegade, and don't forget to tell your crew to wishlist today!
